newsitem.title: USA: Yellow sees further cost cutting. [CORRECTED 17:38 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Yellow sees further cost cutting. [CORRECTED 17:38 GMT]

text.p: Yellow Corp, which earlier reported a third-quarter profit versus a loss, said Thursday the results are unacceptable and further cost cutting is on tap.
"Although we have seen some margin improvement, returns to shareholders remain unacceptable," said A. Maurice Myers, chairman, president and chief executive in a statement.
"Additional steps in restructuring and cost cutting will be taken prior to the end of the year as part of our program to improve profitability," he said.
Yellow earlier said it earned $8.9 million, or $0.32 (Corrects from $0.42) a share, in the third quarter compared to a loss of $11.6 million, or $0.41, in the same period last year.

The transportation company said its Yellow Freight System unit posted operating income of $22.3 million on revenue of $604.5 million. Revenue per ton rose 2.6 percent while cost per ton fell 2.5 percent in the quarter versus a year ago.

"This performance reflects improved revenue as well as cost reduction initiatives, which more than offset a 3.8 percent Teamster wage and benefit increase on April 1 and increased fuel prices," Myers said.
